summary: Iter12 verifies the NEW frontend wiring that surfaces stepped-out escorts inside the 'Stepped Out' column of the Presence Board (in addition to the existing EscortsStrip chip). Backend: 6/6 pytest cases in /app/backend/tests/test_review_iter12.py pass in 2.88s — they confirm the contract /api/presence depends on: active escort with no excursion → temp_out=false/reason=null; POST /api/escort-attendance/temp-exit flips temp_out=true with reason; POST /api/escort-attendance/return flips it back; historical ?on=<past> still returns escorts_present=[]; double step-out is 400; return-without-stepout is 400. Frontend (admin on /presence with seeded Raju Saheb stepped-out for 'Lunch run'): the temp_out column renders (a) the teal 'Escorts' sub-section [data-testid=column-escorts-temp_out], (b) the escort row [data-testid=column-escort-row-7a4c8908-…] with name+institution+since-time+cyan reason 'Lunch run', (c) the 'Es 1' breakdown chip [data-testid=column-breakdown-temp_out-escort], (d) the column-count-temp_out badge reads '1' (= 0 members + 1 escort). The other five columns (on_campus, exited, on_tour, on_leave, absent) do NOT render the Escorts sub-section nor the Es chip — confirmed for all five. On a historical view (date set to today-3), the Read-only history pill renders, the EscortsStrip is hidden, AND the column-escorts-temp_out sub-section + Es chip are also hidden — when navigated back to today via 'Today' button, the sub-section reappears. The stepped-out escort still appears in the EscortsStrip with the cyan escort-presence-stepout-{escort_id} chip (intentional double-surface: strip = roster, column = status).
critical_code_review_comments: Presence.jsx line 235-238: steppedOutEscorts memo `(data?.escorts_present || []).filter((e) => e.temp_out)` is correct — null-safe and reactive. Passed to Column ONLY when col.key === 'temp_out' (line 438) so other columns can never accidentally receive escorts. Good encapsulation.

Column.jsx line 26-31: `Es` breakdown chip pushed conditionally on `escortList.length > 0`. Combined with line 34 `totalCount = members.length + escortList.length`, this is the right shape — the badge surfaces a single combined total and the per-category chips keep the breakdown legible.

Column.jsx line 130-166 EscortRowsSection: rendered at the BOTTOM of the column after all member rows (line 113-115). Visually separated by `bg-teal-50/60 border-y border-teal-200` header. Each row has Avatar, name, institution, since-time, and the temp_out_reason in cyan (Coffee icon at 9px). No click handler — purely informational, as documented.

Column.jsx line 95: `members.length === 0 && escortList.length === 0` guards the empty-state — correct (without the escort check, an escort-only column would show 'No one here.' under the visible escort sub-section).

Presence.jsx line 418: `{!isHistorical && <EscortsStrip ... />}` correctly hides BOTH the strip and (transitively, via steppedOutEscorts being [] in historical mode since data.escorts_present=[]) the column sub-section. No extra guard needed in Column.jsx — the data plumbing already handles it.

Verified via playwright: when no escort is stepped out, the column gracefully falls back to member-only render path (because escortList.length === 0 → no 'Es' chip pushed, no EscortRowsSection rendered, totalCount === members.length). Symmetric and safe.
